sections.title: Cost per DALY equivalent
sections.explainer: Ambitious Impact's headline, from the mean benefit-cost ratio of its simulations ('CEA' tab).

sections.title: The same model at expected values
sections.explainer: The model's yearly costs and benefits with every input at its expected value ('Increasing share to poorest CEA' tab, which matches the 'CEA' tab on everything the ratio depends on), rebuilt so the discount rate can move.

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not Ambitious Impact's: with credit by share of resources on, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost.

sections.title: Bottom line
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not Ambitious Impact's: its bottom line per dollar, in the site's units.

rows.label: Income per person in the receiving country
rows.explainer: Income per person, in dollars, that Ambitious Impact uses to turn money into years of income: the average for sub-Saharan Africa, so its policy ideas compare on one footing.

rows.label: Years of income worth one DALY
rows.explainer: Ambitious Impact counts one DALY as worth 2.8 years of a person's income ("GiveWell/CE moral weight - 1 DALY equal to three years of income"). A year's extra income for one person is close to doubling their consumption for a year, so this is the site's rate between a healthy year and a doubled-income year (Your values). The evaluator view pins it at Ambitious Impact's 2.8.

rows.label: Benefit-cost ratio (mean of 1,000 simulations)
rows.explainer: Ambitious Impact's headline: "a benefit-cost ratio of 38:1, averting the equivalent of a DALY for $288" (report, p. 7). The sheet draws every uncertain input at random 1,000 times and pastes each run's ratio; this is their mean (90% credible interval 4.6 to 111). The runs themselves are pasted numbers; the model's bottom line is the same model at expected values, below.

rows.label: Cost per DALY equivalent, mean of the simulations (AIM's headline; reference only)
rows.explainer: Ambitious Impact's headline, $288 per DALY equivalent, from the simulations' mean ratio. Shown for reference; the model's bottom line is the same calculation at expected values below, like AIM's other 2020 policy models we import, because the simulations are pasted numbers that can't move with the discount rate.

rows.label: Fixed charity costs (first year)
rows.explainer: Ambitious Impact's standard $100,000 to set up a charity.

rows.label: Ongoing charity costs per year
rows.explainer: Four staff at $50,000 plus $50,000 of other costs.

rows.label: Probability the advocacy succeeds
rows.explainer: Ambitious Impact's guess: a 1% chance the charity gets Germany to move part of its bilateral aid from upper-middle- to low-income countries.

rows.label: Share of the change credited to the charity
rows.explainer: Ambitious Impact assumes the policy wouldn't happen without the charity.

rows.label: Germany's bilateral aid budget (2018)
rows.explainer: From OECD data on aid to least developed countries ('ODA to LDCs' tab).

rows.label: Share of the budget moved to low-income countries
rows.explainer: 0.6% of the budget, an assumption chosen so the charity moves about as much as it spends in expectation.

rows.label: How much further money goes in a low-income country
rows.explainer: Money is assumed to do four times as much good in a low-income as in an upper-middle-income country; the money moved away counts against the benefit at a quarter of its value.

rows.label: Yearly return on aid
rows.explainer: "Lower end of average returns" on aid (World Bank; Dalgaard and Hansen).

rows.label: Donor's yearly growth in aid
rows.explainer: OECD forecast of Germany's growth ('Germany GDP' tab).

rows.label: Discount rate
rows.explainer: Ambitious Impact discounts costs and benefits at 4% a year. Linked to the shared discount rate (Your values); the evaluator view pins it to Ambitious Impact's rate.

rows.label: Money moved, net of what it would have done where it was
rows.explainer: The sheet's 'Economic benefit' less its 'Economic disbenefit' (rows 25 and 26): money moved to low-income countries, minus the same money valued at a quarter where it came from.

rows.label: Benefit-cost ratio, all inputs at their expected values
rows.explainer: The same model without the random draws. It is lower than the simulations' mean (38) because the ratio of a skewed quantity averages higher than the ratio at average inputs.

rows.label: Cost per DALY equivalent, at expected values
rows.explainer: AIM's formula (CEA!B37) on the ratio at expected values: about $392 per DALY equivalent. The sheet has no cell for exactly this: its expected-value tab uses an income of $3,794 ($380 per DALY), the main tab $3,919. Its inputs reproduce the sheet.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: From Ambitious Impact's cost note (CEA!F3): "4 staff at 50k each per year plus additional 50k of other costs", so staff are 80% of each year after the first; with the $100,000 setup year counted as non-staff, staff are about 72% of the discounted costs. Range ours.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Researchers and advisers could typically earn considerably more in consulting or industry. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: DALYs averted per dollar
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).

native.unit: $ per DALY equivalent (all inputs at expected values)

summary: Ambitious Impact's 2020 estimate for a new charity persuading Germany to move part of its bilateral aid from upper-middle- to low-income countries, counting the extra income the money produces where it goes further. An earlier AIM model of the aid-quality idea area the Centre for Effective Aid Policy was later founded (from AIM's 2022 report) to work in. A hand re-implementation at expected values, about $392 per DALY equivalent; AIM's headline, $288 (a benefit-cost ratio of 38), is the mean of 1,000 simulations pasted into the sheet and is kept as a reference row.
